title: Chapter 2: The Missing Hours
notes: Playable opening and nonclinical source-review continuation from revised Chapter 2 Scenes 01–02. Owner authorized Chapter 2 implementation; proposed dialogue remains pending narrative review. No new clinical findings, Mara interview, Ward Zero entry or supernatural effect. Work ownership is not clinical completion. The source-question review ends with an unresolved follow-up memo, not a received source packet or completed reconciliation. Both follow-up choices retain all missing information. No new exact event time or approved clinical fact is authored. Scene 04 (Voss institutional review) records factual scope, missing permissions and an authorized follow-up; the pending source request, credential audit and W0-B restriction are unchanged. An urgent safety escalation is feedback-only because no new clinical finding is documented. Scene 03 (Mara Ellis) is owner-approved (2026-10-18) and runs after Scene 04 in this build: clinical interview through the existing dialogue system, EHR note, then a separate referral of her date question to Records. No diagnosis, medication, forensic opinion or treatment effect; Mara is not an evidence source for the hospital inquiry.

objectives.text: Begin the new shift with Naomi at the nursing station.
Review the worklist at the handover board and retain clinical follow-up responsibility.
Compare the maintenance export in Records. Keep the discrepancy unresolved.
Request authorized source records from the office workstation.
Return to Naomi and acknowledge outstanding work.
Review the source-clock questions at the Records worksheet.
Review the repeated minute and export ordering in Records.
Check source independence at the office records-request workstation.
Track preservation and custody confirmation at the office workstation.
Scope the unresolved follow-up memo at the Records worksheet.
Return to Naomi and acknowledge the separate records and clinical follow-ups.
Meet Dr Voss privately and state only what the records establish.
With Dr Voss, identify the permissions the follow-up still needs and who owns them.
Agree an authorized follow-up with Dr Voss.
Interview Mara Ellis in Interview Room A: her records concern, sleep, mood history, alternatives, safety and collateral.
Document Mara's assessment in the EHR. Keep the records question out of the clinical formulation.
Send Mara's date question to Records from the office workstation, separately from her clinical record.

staff_lines.text: Morning, Doctor. The W0-B access ticket is still with Information Security. The useful news is that we have patients to see. I can show you the reports, but do not take my summary as your examination. Keep the clinical work separate from the audit request.
The follow-up is in writing. Records still has your source request, Information Security has the credential question, and the clinical work stays with you and the nursing team.
Doctor. A private word, please, before this becomes a corridor rumour.
Morning, Doctor. Clinical work first. Once your records memo is with Naomi, come and find me.

interactions.title: New-shift worklist
interactions.body: Clinical work remains the priority. Review the existing EHR and retain responsibility for outstanding assessment and follow-up. The administrative audit is a separate work item. This handoff does not replace examination or establish new findings.

options.label: Retain responsibility for clinical review and follow-up
options.response: You retain responsibility for the outstanding clinical review and follow-up. No clinical task is marked completed. The records discrepancy can be investigated separately.

interactions.unavailable_body: Begin the new shift with Naomi before accepting outstanding work.

interactions.title: Maintenance export comparison
interactions.body: Two representations of a maintenance entry display a four-minute discrepancy. One export repeats a minute. The raw time zone, clock source and sort order have not been verified. This is a reported records discrepancy; it does not establish missing time.

options.label: Record the discrepancy as unresolved
options.response: Comparison recorded as unresolved. Request the authorized source-system export and preservation of the originals before drawing conclusions.

interactions.unavailable_body: Confirm who owns the outstanding clinical review at the handover board before pursuing the audit.
interactions.completed_body: The initial mismatch is recorded as unresolved. Continue the source-clock review at this worksheet.

interactions.title: Authorized source request
interactions.body: Request preservation of the original records and an authorized source-system export. Ask for the raw offsets, clock source and sort order. Making a request does not grant access or authenticate a record.

options.label: Submit preservation and source-export request
options.response: Request submitted for authorized Records review. Source access and reconciliation remain pending. The originals must be retained; no independent corroboration or loss of time is established.

interactions.unavailable_body: Record the comparison as unresolved in Records before requesting source material.
interactions.completed_body: The preservation and export request is submitted. Receipt, custody and source independence still need verification.

interactions.title: New-shift handoff
interactions.body:
Bennett: We have patients to see. Keep the clinical work moving while Records checks the source material.

The audit request remains unresolved. You retain the outstanding clinical work.

options.label: Acknowledge the outstanding work and records follow-up
options.response: Handoff acknowledged. Clinical review remains assigned to you, and the source-export request remains with Records. Continue routine care while the source material is reconciled.

interactions.unavailable_body: The source request is not yet recorded. Clinical review remains separate from the audit.
interactions.completed_body: Clinical review remains assigned separately from the unresolved records inquiry.

interactions.title: Records worksheet: source clocks
interactions.body:
[b]Reported comparison[/b]
Two representations display a four-minute difference; an export repeats a minute.

[b]Available clock metadata[/b]
Raw time-zone offset: unverified.
Source clock and synchronization authority: unverified.
No authorized raw export has been received in this review.

What correction can this comparison support?

options.label: Apply a four-minute correction to reconcile the records
options.response: A displayed difference alone does not establish a clock correction. The source offsets and clock authority are still unverified. Retain the original representations and review the missing metadata.

options.label: Keep the correction unknown and request clock authority
options.response: Clock review recorded: no correction can be justified yet. Raw offsets, clock authority and synchronization history remain requested. The displayed mismatch remains unresolved.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Clock authority and raw offsets remain unverified. Continue with the export-order review at this worksheet.

interactions.title: Records worksheet: export order
interactions.body:
[b]Reported export[/b]
A minute appears more than once.

[b]Missing information[/b]
Raw event sequence, export sort key and transformation history have not been verified. A display row is not proof of an elapsed interval.

How should the repeated minute be recorded?

options.label: Classify the repeated minute as proven missing time
options.response: That conclusion exceeds the available source material. Repeated display values can only be recorded as a discrepancy while ordering and transformation history remain unverified.

options.label: Retain the repeated row and request raw ordering metadata
options.response: Export-order review recorded. Preserve the original representation and request its sort key, raw event sequence and transformation history. Do not reorder or overwrite the original.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Clock and export-order gaps are recorded. Review source dependencies at the office records-request workstation.

interactions.title: Source review: independence
interactions.body:
[b]Current material[/b]
The two displayed representations have not been traced to independently acquired originals. Source extraction, clock dependencies and transformation lineage remain unverified.

Would receiving another copy establish independent corroboration?

options.label: Count another copy as independent corroboration
options.response: A copy can preserve or reproduce a source; it does not by itself establish independence. Shared originals, clocks and export pipelines still need to be checked. No evidence status has been promoted.

options.label: Leave independence unestablished and request the source lineage
options.response: Dependency review recorded: source independence remains unestablished. Request original capture, clock authority, extraction history and shared dependencies before counting corroboration.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Source independence remains unestablished. Check the preservation request at this workstation.

interactions.title: Source review: preservation and custody
interactions.body:
[b]Request status[/b]
Preservation and an authorized source-system export have been requested.

[b]Outstanding confirmation[/b]
No original receipt, immutable checksum or custody acknowledgment is supplied by the current comparison. A request is not confirmation that preservation occurred.

How should the request be tracked?

options.label: Mark the originals as preserved because the request was sent
options.response: Sending the request does not confirm custody or preservation. Keep confirmation outstanding and retain the request without claiming receipt of an original.

options.label: Keep preservation confirmation and source receipt outstanding
options.response: Preservation follow-up recorded. Request confirmation of original receipt, unchanged source bytes/checksum and custody history from authorized Records staff. Receipt and preservation remain unconfirmed.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Preservation confirmation, raw export receipt and custody remain outstanding. Return to the Records worksheet to scope the follow-up memo.

interactions.title: Unresolved records memo
interactions.body:
[b]Reported[/b]
Four-minute displayed mismatch; repeated minute in an export.

[b]Still unknown[/b]
Clock authority and offsets; raw event ordering; extraction lineage and shared dependencies; original receipt, checksum and custody confirmation.

[b]Standing[/b]
Discrepancy unresolved. No proven loss of time, independent corroboration or patient finding. Preserve the original representations and keep clinical documentation separate.

Choose the emphasis for the next authorized follow-up. Both requests retain all outstanding source questions.

options.label: Prioritize clock authority and raw offsets in the follow-up
options.response: Unresolved memo recorded with clock-authority/offset verification prioritized. Records must also address ordering, lineage, custody and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.

options.label: Prioritize source lineage and custody in the follow-up
options.response: Unresolved memo recorded with source-lineage/custody verification prioritized. Records must also address clock authority, offsets, ordering and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: The unresolved memo retains the reported mismatch and all missing source questions. An authorized technical follow-up is requested; original receipt, preservation and reconciliation remain pending. No independent corroboration or missing-time conclusion is recorded.

interactions.title: Records follow-up handoff
interactions.body:
Bennett: Keep the records questions with the authorized review. The clinical work still needs its own follow-up.

The comparison remains unresolved. Source receipt, clock verification and preservation confirmation remain outstanding. Your clinical responsibilities have not been marked completed by this inquiry.

options.label: Acknowledge the records follow-up and separate clinical responsibility
options.response: Records-review handoff acknowledged. The unresolved memo and authorized follow-up remain recorded. Continue clinical work separately; source material and technical reconciliation are still outstanding.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: institutional review
interactions.body:
Voss steps aside where the corridor is quiet.

Voss: An incomplete entry can become an allegation very quickly. I'm not asking you to ignore it. I'm asking you to tell me what was actually established.

[b]On record[/b]
A transfer request to W0-B was logged under a staff credential marked inactive. The requester was not identified.
A four-minute displayed mismatch and a repeated minute in a maintenance export are recorded as unresolved. Your source request is pending with Records.

What do you tell her?

options.label: Say someone deliberately used the inactive credential
options.response: Voss: Who? The audit shows a credential, not a person. Write that someone did it on purpose and you have made an allegation the record does not support. Tell me what was established.

options.label: Say the export proves the ward lost four minutes
options.response: Voss: Records has not verified the clock source or the export order. A displayed mismatch is a discrepancy, not a missing interval. What do you actually have?

options.label: State only what is established, and what is not
options.response:
Player: An inactive credential appears in an archived transfer-request audit. It doesn't identify the person who used it. The export mismatch is reported and unresolved; clock authority, ordering, lineage and preservation are unverified.

Voss: Good. Document patient-safety concerns separately from information-security concerns. They have different owners.

Factual scope recorded. Talk to Voss again about what the follow-up still needs.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: missing permissions
interactions.body:
Voss: Then separate the owners. What does the follow-up still need, and who has to authorize it?

[b]Factual scope[/b]
Inactive credential in a transfer-request audit; user not identified. Export discrepancy unresolved; source request pending with Records.

[b]Your current authority[/b]
Attending clinical access only. No credential-audit authority, no source-system access and no authorization for W0-B.

options.label: Ask Voss to authorize you to inspect W0-B yourself
options.response: Voss: No. W0-B is Security's door, and any inspection needs their authorization and an escort. A records question is not a reason to open a sealed ward. Your access is unchanged.

options.label: Ask for direct access to the raw source system
options.response: Voss: That isn't mine to hand out, and it shouldn't be yours to take. Records holds the source export; Information Security holds the credential audit. Your request stays with them.

options.label: Record the missing permissions and their owners
options.response:
Missing permissions recorded:
Information Security: audit of the inactive credential and who could use it.
Records: the pending preservation and source-export request, with clock and ordering metadata.
Security: any question about W0-B access policy. No inspection is authorized.
Clinical follow-up stays with you and the nursing team.

Voss: That is a list I can send to people who can act on it. Now tell me what you want to happen next.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: authorized follow-up
interactions.body:
Voss: What do you want to happen next? Pick something I can authorize today.

[b]Still pending[/b]
Records source request, preservation confirmation and reconciliation. Information Security credential audit. No new clinical finding has been documented in this review.

options.label: Press for an urgent patient-safety escalation
options.response: Voss: On what finding? Nothing in this review documents a new risk to a patient. If your clinical assessment identifies one, escalate it through clinical channels at once and I will back you. It does not ride on an audit memo. Choose a follow-up the record supports.

options.label: Request the written escalation process
options.response:
Voss: Reasonable. I'll send you the incident-escalation procedure and copy the Records and Information Security leads. Your source request stays open with Records; nothing is closed by this.

Follow-up recorded: written process requested. The records discrepancy and the credential audit remain unresolved.

options.label: Propose an independent records reconciliation
options.response:
Voss: I'd rather Records finished its own work first. But a neutral second review is a fair request, and I'll put it to the quality committee in writing. It does not replace your pending request.

Follow-up recorded: independent reconciliation proposed. The source request, preservation confirmation and credential audit remain pending.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Records referral: Mara Ellis's question
interactions.body:
[b]Request[/b]
Mara Ellis asks for two copies of her aunt Lillian Ellis's 1988 record to be checked: a paper record dated October 12 and a later archive copy dated October 14.

[b]Separation[/b]
This is an administrative records question. It is not part of the hospital's W0-B inquiry, and Mara's clinical assessment stays in the EHR.

How should it be sent?

options.label: Attach your clinical assessment to support her request
options.response: Records does not need her clinical details to compare two copies. Send only what the question requires; her assessment stays confidential in the EHR.

options.label: Add the date conflict to the W0-B records inquiry
options.response: Mara is a patient with her own question, not a source for the hospital's inquiry. Nothing links her aunt's record to W0-B. Refer it on its own.

options.label: Refer the date question to Records on its own
options.response: Referral sent to the authorized Records office: two copies, two dates, origin of each copy to be checked. No finding about the records is made, and nothing in Mara's clinical assessment changes. Her follow-up (sleep and function support, safety follow-up, legal-role clarification, medication reconciliation) stays with the clinical team.

interactions.unavailable_body: Document Mara's assessment in the EHR first. Her records question is referred separately.
interactions.completed_body: Mara's date question is with Records, separate from her clinical record. No finding about the copies has been made.

sign_out.title: Clinical handoff
sign_out.undocumented_message: Outstanding clinical review still requires an appropriate handoff.
